newsitem.title: USA: Senator charges China with U.S. campaign plan.
newsitem.headline: Senator charges China with U.S. campaign plan.

text.p: Senate Governmental Affairs Committee chairman Fred Thompson charged on Tuesday that China had a plan to use contributions to U.S. political campaigns to advance its goals in relations with the United States.

"The committee believes that high-level Chinese government officials crafted a plan to increase China's influence over the U.S. political process," he said, opening hearings into the financing of President Bill Clinton's 1996 presidential campaign and other campaign funding irregularities.

His Democratic counterpart, Sen. John Glenn, warned against a "jump to conclusions," based upon news reports of China's efforts to use funds to lobby the U.S. Congress. He countered that the investigation should look at foreign money contributed to both Republican and Democratic parties.
"Is there any real evidence that the Chinese government, or any other other foreign government, actually infiltrated the American government via campaign contributions?" the Ohio senator said.

Glenn noted that the only known lobbying activity by China was legitimate and of the type many countries conduct in the United States to influence foreign policy. He noted that news reports this year said China planned to use about $2 million to gain influence by focusing on Congress.

Thompson said Clinton's decision to grant a visa to Taiwan's President Lee Teng-hui to visit his former college, Cornell University, in 1996 after pressure from Congress caught Beijing "off-guard" and led to its decision to become involved in U.S. politics.
